extracted.intended_audience: federal executive agencies (agency heads, counsel, procurement officials), United States Trade Representative, agency implementers of NAFTA provisions
extracted.subtask_description: Executive Order implementing NAFTA obligations across Federal agencies, specifying procedural requirements for rule publication, procurement, patent use, and agency responsibilities. Directs agencies on timing, waivers, definitions, and internal procedures to conform with NAFTA and related statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of United States Section of the NAFTA Secretariat
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to section 105(a) of the NAFTA Implementation Act, a United States section of the NAFTA Secretariat shall be established within the Department of Commerce and shall carry out the functions set out in that section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of binational panel and committee decisions by the President
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to subparagraph 516A(g)(7)(B) of the Tariff Act of 1930, in the event that the provisions of that subparagraph take effect, the President accepts, as a whole, all decisions of binational panels and extraordinary challenge committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for publication/notice of proposed Federal technical regulations and sanitary or phytosanitary measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency subject to the Administrative Procedure Act shall, in applying section 553 of title 5, publish or serve notice of any proposed Federal technical regulation or any Federal sanitary or phytosanitary measure of general application not less than 75 days before the comment due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to proposed Federal technical regulations and sanitary/phytosanitary measures of general application, except as provided in specified exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — Technical regulations relating to perishable goods
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a technical regulation relating to perishable goods, the agency shall, to the greatest extent practicable, publish or serve notice at least 30 days prior to adoption of such regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit shorter-timing exception to the 75-day publication requirement for perishable goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — Urgent technical regulations for safety/environment/consumers
rubrics_metrics.description: For a technical regulation where the United States considers it necessary to address an urgent problem relating to safety or to protection of human, animal or plant life or health, the environment or consumers, the 75-day timing requirement does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may adopt expedited timing when addressing urgent safety, health, environmental, or consumer-protection problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — Urgent sanitary or phytosanitary measures
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a sanitary or phytosanitary measure where the United States considers it necessary to address an urgent problem relating to sanitary or phytosanitary protection, the 75-day timing requirement does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may expedite sanitary/phytosanitary measures when an urgent protection need exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of 'sanitary or phytosanitary measure' and 'technical regulation'
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the publication/notice provisions, 'sanitary or phytosanitary measure' shall be defined in accordance with section 463 of the Trade Agreements Act of 1979, and 'technical regulation' shall be defined in accordance with section 473 of the Trade Agreements Act of 1979.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must use the statutory definitions from the Trade Agreements Act when applying the notice/timing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supersession of Executive Order No. 12662
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4 of this order supersedes section 1 of Executive Order No. 12662 of December 31, 1988.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that prior EO guidance is displaced to the extent specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement waiver for eligible Canadian and Mexican products and suppliers
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to eligible products of Canada and Mexico, and suppliers of such products, the application of any law, regulation, procedure, or practice regarding Federal Government procurement that would result in treatment less favorable than the most favorable treatment accorded (A) to United States products and services and suppliers of such products and services; or (B) to eligible products of either Mexico or Canada, shall be waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a stand-alone waiver instructing agencies to avoid less-favorable treatment of eligible NAFTA products/suppliers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of procurement waiver by agencies listed in Annexes 1 and 2
rubrics_metrics.description: This waiver shall be applied by all executive agencies listed in Annexes 1 and 2 of this Executive order in consultation with, and when deemed necessary at the direction of, the United States Trade Representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies specified in the annexes must implement the waiver in coordination with the USTR and follow USTR direction when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of Defense determinations for Article 1018(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of Defense, or his designee, in consultation with the Trade Representative, shall be responsible for determinations under Article 1018(1), pursuant to Annex 1001.1b–1(A)(4), of the NAFTA, and shall establish procedures for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigns explicit responsibility and requires establishment of procedures for defense-related procurement determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies in Annex 2 directed to procure eligible products consistent with NAFTA Chapter 10 procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive agencies listed in Annex 2 are directed to procure eligible products in compliance with the procedural provisions of Chapter 10 of the NAFTA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure their procurement processes conform to the Chapter 10 procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade Representative responsible for calculating and adjusting NAFTA threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trade Representative shall be responsible for calculating and adjusting the threshold as required by Article 1001(1)(c) of the NAFTA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USTR handles threshold determination for procurement coverage under NAFTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of procurement order to solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: This order shall apply only to solicitations issued on or after the date of entry into force of the NAFTA for the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procurement waiver and related duties do not apply retroactively to solicitations issued before NAFTA entry into force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim implementation pending FAR revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Although regulatory implementation of this order must await revisions to the Federal Acquisitions Regulation (FAR), it is expected that agencies listed in Annexes 1 and 2 will take all appropriate actions in the interim to implement those aspects of the order that are not dependent upon regulatory revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should act promptly on implementable items even before formal FAR amendments are completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council incorporation timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to section 25 of the Office of Federal Procurement Policy Act, as amended (41 U.S.C. 421(a)), the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council shall ensure that the policies established herein are incorporated in the FAR within 30 days from the date this order is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAR Council has a 30-day deadline to incorporate the order's policies into the FAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency procedures for Government use of patented technology (notice requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall, within 30 days from the date this order is issued, modify or adopt procedures to ensure compliance with Article 1709(10) of the NAFTA regarding notice when patented technology is used by or for the Federal Government without a license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must act within 30 days to establish notice procedures for use of patented technology by or for the Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of 'reasonable efforts to obtain advance authorization' requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement of Article 1709(10)(b) regarding reasonable efforts to obtain advance authorization from the patent owner is waived for an invention used or manufactured by or for the Federal Government, except that the patent owner must be notified whenever the agency or its contractor, without making a patent search, knows or has demonstrable reasonable grounds to know that an invention described in and covered by a valid United States patent is or will be used or manufactured without a license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance authorization obligation is waived but a notification duty remains whenever the agency/contractor knows or reasonably should know of the patent coverage; notification must occur even if no patent search was done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of advance authorization in national emergency or extreme urgency
rubrics_metrics.description: The advance authorization requirement is waived whenever a national emergency or other circumstances of extreme urgency exists, except that the patent owner must be notified as soon as it is reasonably practicable to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In emergencies, agencies may proceed without prior authorization but must notify patent owners promptly when practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of 'remuneration' for patented technology used by Government
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall treat the term 'remuneration' as used in Articles 1709(10)(h) and (j) and 1715 of the NAFTA as equivalent to 'reasonable and entire compensation' as used in section 1498 of title 28, United States Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes equivalence in terminology to align NAFTA language with domestic compensation standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice does not constitute admission of infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this order is intended to suggest that the giving of notice to a patent owner under Article 1709(10) of the NAFTA constitutes an admission that the Federal Government has infringed a valid privately-owned patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification obligations are procedural and do not imply legal admission of infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: No creation of enforceable rights by the order (Judicial review)
rubrics_metrics.description: This order does not create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law by a party against the United States, its agencies, its officers, or any person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms that the EO itself does not create private causes of action or enforceable legal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date tied to NAFTA entry into force
rubrics_metrics.description: This order shall take effect upon the date of entry into force of the NAFTA for the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All timing and applicability provisions are keyed to NAFTA's entry into force date for the U.S.
